decode.note: greedy is tier 2's measured degenerate case and is never used

disclosures: single training run — no seed-level clustering is possible and none is claimed
MOVEMENT claim about the generative distribution, never a question-quality claim and never 'novel questions help students'.
On a 50-question corpus partial memorisation is EXPECTED; the memorisation panel reports it rather than hiding it.
Manifold support 0.90 is a reference line, not a gate; a failure is a result.
The instruments are the mind-model's own codec/EPIG, by design; this is not an independent judgement of question quality.
Tuned no-history rows are OUT OF THE TRAINING DISTRIBUTION: under the warm draw (§4.8) the tuned model never saw an empty history. Reference line only.

Rung A's Û instrument validation used the OLD COLD DRAW (start 0, 11.1% cold rows). It stands as registered because it is an instrument-validation claim and not a personalisation claim -- but the draws did not match, and this says so.

PRIMARY pointing is the realised-r percentile of the projected menu item. EPIG percentile is SECONDARY: rung A measured Spearman(EPIG, true r) within a state at only 0.07-0.10, so an EPIG-percentile null is NOT evidence that the signal failed to shape generation -- the training signal is r, and the panel scores against it.

The no-history arm is 110 generations per model (one per learner, reused across that learner's starts). The no-history prompt is a single identical string, so the former 440 rows were resamples of it; pairing was by index under matched batch seeds and never true CRN, and the bootstrap is learner-clustered, so no statistic changes meaning.

History-sensitivity's HEADLINE is the swapped-history contrast, not history-vs-no-history: every history block prints the completed exercise's own statement and CW's assignment order is fixed, so a with/without gap is substantially curriculum position rather than the person.
